clue.text: Horse from European Union gasps, having had treatment

indicators.note: letters that have been treated are worked over and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A horse from Europe gasps for breath after veterinary treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having had treatment' rearranges EU plus GASPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged steed of Greek myth is the most famous horse in legend.

clue.text: Party lifted for time in party skit

indicators.note: for signals one thing replacing another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party sketch is put on at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns DO into OD, which replaces T in PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic imitation or send-up is a skit.

clue.text: Spring seen in spring?

definitions.meaning: to spring is to leap or frolic
lambs leaping about are a familiar sight in springtime

explanation.surface: A question about what happens in the season of spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip and leap about playfully, as lambs do in the spring.

clue.text: Grant horse is running, but over a limited distance

indicators.note: running signals the letters are on the move, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Grant's horse is running, but only a short race.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile or forecast reaching only a short distance is described this way.

clue.text: Acknowledge mistake while on one's feet

definitions.meaning: ... and having been put right, taken literally

explanation.surface: Admitting an error while standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept that one has been shown to be wrong.

clue.text: PC has yen to act out a kind of murder

parts.note: a police constable is a cop
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

indicators.note: out signals the word act is put out of order

explanation.surface: A police constable is tempted to act out a particular sort of killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ACT into CAT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime imitating an earlier well-publicised killing is described with this adjective, as in a copying murder.

clue.text: Lamentations? Not 28!

parts.note: laments that are not genuine, as the clue at 28 says; Lamentations is also a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Questioning whether some weeping is heartfelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across is SINCERE, so these are insincere laments.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere grief shown for effect is named after the reptile said to weep while eating its prey.

clue.text: Stiffly formal, but with a soft edge

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
an edge is a rim

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and formal, but with a gentler side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stiffly proper and correct is prim.

clue.text: Wallop — and then gin? Nonsense!

parts.note: a clap is a blow or wallop
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A drink of wallop beer followed by gin, a silly idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is also slang for beer, and gin a drink, but here gin means a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, pretentious talk designed to win applause is rubbish.

clue.text: A little bit thrown out by the heat

definitions.text: A little bit thrown out by the heat

parts.words: A little bit thrown out by the heat
parts.note: a tiny charged particle emitted from a heated body

explanation.surface: Something small rejected because of the hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion or electron emitted from a hot substance has this physics name.

clue.text: Aggressive man from crowd at the box office

parts.note: to crowd is to cram or ram together

explanation.surface: A tough guy draws the crowds at the box office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crowd' looks like a noun but works as a verb meaning to pack in.
explanation.definitionFit: The film character played by Stallone has become a byword for a violently macho type.

clue.text: Detest a crowd being about in tea breaks

indicators.note: being turned about means the word for crowd is read backwards

parts.note: a crowd is a mob

indicators.note: breaks signals the word tea is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the throng that gathers during tea breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being about' turns MOB into BOM; 'breaks' turns TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is a direct synonym of this verb.

clue.text: Don't be entranced by such a salesman!

definitions.text: Don't be entranced by such a salesman!

parts.words: Don't be entranced by such a salesman!
parts.note: entranced is read as en-tranced, let past the entrance by a seller who goes from house to house calling

explanation.surface: A warning not to be charmed by a pushy salesman's patter.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman who calls at each house in turn is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Check stock

definitions.meaning: to check is to stop or stanch a flow
a stock is the main stalk or trunk of a plant

explanation.surface: An instruction to verify inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to staunch a flow, and the main stalk of a plant.

clue.text: He could be interested in the bar and a glass

definitions.text: He could be interested in the bar and a glass

parts.words: He could be interested in the bar and a glass
parts.note: the bar is a unit of pressure and a glass is a barometer, both of interest to a forecaster rather than a drinker

explanation.surface: A man who likes the pub and a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster studies pressure readings on the barometer to predict conditions.

clue.text: Group of islands with a pair, eg having loch incorporated

indicators.note: the letters are all incorporated together into one mixed body, then reformed

explanation.surface: A chain of islands, paired up, contains a Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporated' mixes A, PAIR, EG and LOCH together; 'with' and 'having' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names a cluster or chain of islands in the sea.

clue.text: See 4
One with a place to rest — a little one, not exactly great

definitions.text: One with a place to rest

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, a place to rest for a little one

indicators.note: not exactly signals the word great is inexact, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a small resting place, though not a grand one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a small country house, their home.

clue.text: Provided nourishment round trees, decayed and rotted

indicators.note: round signals the first word goes around the other

parts.note: fed means provided nourishment

indicators.note: decayed signals the word trees is broken down and rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeding trees made them decay and rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decayed' looks like part of the definition but it signals the anagram; 'round' puts the shuffled trees inside, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that has gone bad and putrefied has rotted.

clue.text: It's regularly worn outside

parts.note: an item of clothing put on over the rest, as a coat is when going out

explanation.surface: Something habitually worn out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' tempts you to take alternate letters, but none give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat or cloak worn over other clothes is a garment of this sort.

clue.text: Breather in the exercises required for a dive

indicators.note: in signals the breather goes inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
a lung is a breathing organ

explanation.surface: Breathing exercises needed before diving.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong dive into water is a plunge.

clue.text: Casually go in; it's an easy thing to do

definitions.meaning: to enter in a casual, carefree way
a simple task is a doddle or cinch

explanation.surface: Wandering in casually; nothing to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To waltz in, and also a task so easy it is like a light wind.

clue.text: Flap when head overlooked the art centre

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is overlooked, so it is dropped

parts.note: being in a flap is being in a state

explanation.surface: A panic arises when the boss is ignored at the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when head overlooked' drops the first letter of STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries, Tate Modern being the best known.

clue.text: Superior selection of wines, we hear, which has sold a lot

parts.note: superior means best

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a wine collection is a cellar

explanation.surface: A fine wine collection that has proved very popular with buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: CELLAR said out loud sounds like SELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or product that sells in very large numbers earns this label.

clue.text: See 5
Friend for tea

explanation.surface: Asking a pal over for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal, and the South American herbal infusion made from holly leaves.

clue.text: Character featuring largely in book by Rabelais

definitions.text: Character featuring largely in book by Rabelais

parts.words: Character featuring largely in book by Rabelais
parts.note: largely hints at a giant, the hero of the French writer's sixteenth-century comic book

explanation.surface: A figure prominent in a work by the French satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelais's novel follows a huge giant, which is also the root of the word gargantuan.

clue.text: Part of the churchman's emolument?

indicators.note: part of signals the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about what a clergyman's pay includes.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across churchMAN'S Emolument; a minister's house often came with the living, so the clue defines too.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's house was traditionally provided as part of his stipend or living.

clue.text: Had reed camouflaged this duck?

indicators.note: something camouflaged is disguised, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Could a duck hide among the reeds?
explanation.walkthrough: 'camouflaged' rearranges HAD and REED; 'this' points to the duck being the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North American diving duck with a reddish head.

clue.text: Church in error about what's true

indicators.note: in signals that the church abbreviation goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sin is an error or wrongdoing
re means about, concerning
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church is in error about what is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church in error' tempts you to put the church inside the error alone, but it goes inside both following pieces; 'what's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartfelt, genuine feeling is a true one.
